newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran, Tajikistan expel diplomats in spy row.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Tajikistan expel diplomats in spy row.

text.p: Iran has ordered out a Tajik diplomat in retaliation for Tajikistan's expulsion of an Iranian diplomat in an apparent spy row, Iranian media said on Tuesday.

The daily Kayhan said Iran's foreign ministry on Monday summoned the Tajik charge d'affaires and handed him an expulsion order for an unnamed embassy attache for allegedly engaging in "activities not consistent with his diplomatic status."
Iran's state radio said Tajikistan on Monday ordered an Iranian diplomat to leave the central Asian country.
Embassy political expert Morteza Moussavi was expelled for allegedly "exchanging information", the radio said in its English-language broadcast. It did not elaborate.
Tehran-Dushanbe ties were strained in June when Tajik President Imomali Rahmonov accused Iran of being among states training rebel forces. Tehran denied the charge.

Iran, which shares a common language with Tajikistan, has repeatedly called for talks between the Tajik government and the Islamic rebels who have waged a guerrilla war since their defeat in a 1992 civil war.
